title: Purposes of Life: 9 Commands / Commands 8th and 9th, and Summary

questions.question: What is the eighth aim of human life in this passage?
questions.answer: It is to understand how the creatures in the world point to Allah’s oneness and His caring rule, each in its own way.

questions.question: What does “each in its particular tongue” mean here?
questions.answer: It means each created thing shows this message in its own special manner, not necessarily with spoken words.

questions.question: What is the ninth aim of life?
questions.answer: It is to learn about Allah’s power and richness by noticing our own weakness, poverty, and need.

questions.question: How does the passage use hunger to explain this idea?
questions.answer: It shows that just as people understand food better when they feel hunger, they can better understand Allah’s power and provision by feeling their own need.

questions.question: What should a person understand through his weakness?
questions.answer: He should understand the greatness of Allah’s power.

questions.question: What should a person understand through his poverty and need?
questions.answer: He should understand the vastness of Allah’s riches and generosity.

questions.question: After listing the eighth and ninth aims, what does the passage say about the aims of life as a whole?
questions.answer: It says these are examples that briefly summarize the aims of life.

questions.question: What does the passage tell the reader to consider next?
questions.answer: It tells the reader to think about the nature of life.

questions.question: In the passage, what are people supposed to understand from the beings in the world?
questions.answer: They are supposed to understand the message those beings give about Allah’s unity and lordship.

questions.question: Does the passage present the world as silent or as full of signs?
questions.answer: It presents the world as full of signs.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention different “tongues” for created things?
questions.answer: To show that many kinds of creatures teach about Allah in different ways.

questions.question: What human qualities are named as a way to learn about Allah?
questions.answer: Weakness, helplessness, poverty, and need.

questions.question: What can a person learn about Allah by recognizing helplessness?
questions.answer: He can learn how great Allah’s power is.

questions.question: What can a person learn about Allah by recognizing need?
questions.answer: He can learn how unlimited Allah’s wealth and care are.

questions.question: What everyday example is used to make this easier to understand?
questions.answer: The example of hunger and the enjoyment of food.

questions.question: How does hunger help explain the lesson?
questions.answer: Hunger makes a person notice flavors and levels of satisfaction, just as need helps a person notice Allah’s gifts and power.

questions.question: What transition happens at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: It moves from the aims of life to a new part about the nature of life.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is one duty of a person when looking at the world?
questions.answer: It is to understand what creation is showing about Allah.

questions.question: What two truths are creation said to speak about?
questions.answer: Allah’s oneness and His lordship over creation.

questions.question: What does the passage say we should notice about ourselves?
questions.answer: We should notice our weakness, need, and lack.

questions.question: Why is noticing our limits important?
questions.answer: Because it helps us understand Allah’s perfect power and endless riches.

questions.question: What comparison is made with food?
questions.answer: Different levels of hunger help people understand enjoyment of food, just as different needs help people understand Allah’s gifts.

questions.question: Does the passage teach self-sufficiency or dependence on Allah?
questions.answer: It teaches dependence on Allah.

questions.question: How are the aims of life described after the eighth and ninth points?
questions.answer: They are described as a brief summary of important matters.

questions.question: What is the next topic introduced right before the passage ends?
questions.answer: The nature of life.

questions.question: What is the eighth item in the list about?
questions.answer: It is about understanding the message of all created things about Allah.

questions.question: Which two ideas about Allah are especially mentioned in that item?
questions.answer: His oneness and His ruling care over creation.

questions.question: What is the ninth item mainly about?
questions.answer: It is about using our own weakness and need to understand Allah better.

questions.question: Which human conditions are named in the ninth item?
questions.answer: Helplessness, weakness, poverty, and need.

questions.question: Which divine qualities are understood through those conditions?
questions.answer: Allah’s power and His great riches.

questions.question: Why does the passage bring up hunger?
questions.answer: Because hunger is an easy example that shows how a need can help a person understand a blessing more deeply.

questions.question: What does the phrase “briefly, are matters like these” show about the list?
questions.answer: It shows the list is a summary, not a complete explanation of everything.

questions.question: After finishing the list, what question is the reader guided to think about?
questions.answer: The reader is guided to think about what life itself is like in its nature.

questions.question: What should a believer understand from the world around him, according to the eighth point?
questions.answer: He should understand that creation points to Allah’s oneness and His authority over all things.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the creatures of the world?
questions.answer: They are like signs that teach important truths about Allah.

questions.question: In the ninth point, what four things about humans are mentioned?
questions.answer: Powerlessness, weakness, poverty, and need.

questions.question: What do those four things help a person realize about Allah?
questions.answer: They help him realize Allah’s perfect strength and unlimited wealth.

questions.question: How does the food example make the lesson clearer?
questions.answer: It shows that need helps people notice value, just as spiritual need helps people notice Allah’s greatness.

questions.question: Why is it important that the passage says Allah’s power and riches are infinite?
questions.answer: It shows that Allah has no limit, while human beings are limited.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the aims of life at the end of this section?
questions.answer: It describes them as a short summary of important purposes.

questions.question: What new subject begins in the last line of the target passage?
questions.answer: A discussion of the nature of life begins.

questions.question: What is the eighth purpose of life mentioned here?
questions.answer: It is to understand the testimony of the created world about Allah’s unity and lordship.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by the world speaking in many “tongues”?
questions.answer: It means different parts of creation show the truth in different forms.

questions.question: What is the ninth purpose of life in this section?
questions.answer: It is to learn about Allah’s power and richness through our own weakness and need.

questions.question: Why are weakness and need not useless according to this passage?
questions.answer: They help a person recognize Allah’s greatness and turn to Him.

questions.question: What example from daily life is used to explain different degrees?
questions.answer: The example of hunger and how it affects enjoyment of food.

questions.question: What is similar between hunger for food and human need before Allah?
questions.answer: Both help a person notice value more clearly.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the list of life’s aims after giving the ninth one?
questions.answer: It says the aims of life, in short, are like these matters.

questions.question: What sentence shows the passage is about to move to a new topic?
questions.answer: The line that tells the reader to think next about the nature of life.
